details: No built-in fallback. retryandreflect plugin retries tool errors not model errors. You write an OnModelErrorCallback to retry on different model. Native providers limited to Gemini + Apigee Vertex.

First-class FallbackConfig in libs/agno/agno/models/fallback.py:20-40 with separate fallback lists for on_error, on_rate_limit, on_context_overflow plus optional callback for instrumentation. Shortcut Agent(fallback_models=[...]). 49 native providers.

First-class FallbackLayer in crates/autoagents-llm/src/optim/fallback.rs:64. Composes with RetryLayer via PipelineBuilder. default_is_fallbackable classifies HttpError, ProviderError, NoToolSupport as fallback-eligible; Auth and InvalidRequest propagate.

fallback_model: str on ClaudeAgentOptions (types.py:1679-1680) is single-step only, not a multi-rung chain. On overage/outage the underlying CLI falls back. ResultMessage.model_usage shows the split. Anthropic-only providers.

Options.fallbackModel (sdk.d.ts:1301) is single-step fallback triggered by API errors and rate-limit responses, not a chain of N models. Issue #313 requests exposing retry policy controls. Anthropic providers via gateway abstraction (firstParty/bedrock/vertex/foundry/etc).

No built-in cross-provider fallback. max_retry_limit=2 on Agent (agent/core.py:242) retries the same task on error but does not switch models. Workaround is LiteLLM's intra-provider retries. Native SDKs for OpenAI/Anthropic/Azure/Bedrock/Gemini plus LiteLLM.

ModelRetryConfig (adk/chatmodel.go:307) retries on the same model with backoff; not a fallback chain. To fall back to a different model you write a WrapModel that catches errors and dispatches to a backup. 11 first-party adapters.

Fallback middleware (plugins/middleware/fallback.go:59-70) accepts an ordered ModelRef list; triggers on UNAVAILABLE, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, INTERNAL etc. with configurable Statuses. Composes with Retry middleware (exponential backoff + jitter) in Retry{Fallback{model}} pattern.

langchain-core Runnable.with_fallbacks([fallback_model, ...]) is usable on the model passed to create_react_agent. Fires on Exception; you encode policy yourself. No built-in retry-on-rate-limit-with-different-provider semantic.

Not first-class in core. There is a Cloudflare AI Gateway integration that provides fallback, and you can wrap an LLM with retry/fallback yourself. 104 LLM integrations but no built-in fallback primitive.

loop() takes a models array (packages/core/src/loop/loop.ts:13); if the first model fails Mastra retries on the next. MODEL_GENERATION spans are re-stamped if a fallback served the request. No per-error-category classification like agno.

MAF does not ship a fallback decorator. Microsoft.Extensions.AI ecosystem has DistributedCachingChatClient and LoggingChatClient decorators and community-provided fallback decorators exist, but nothing first-class in MAF itself.

RetryPolicy (src/agents/retry.py) wraps individual model calls with structured retry advice including ModelRetryAdvice and ModelRetryBackoffSettings. Cross-provider fallback is BYO: wrap Runner.run in try/except and re-run with different RunConfig.model. No with_fallbacks builder.

getResponseWithRetry / getStreamedResponseWithRetry in packages/agents-core/src/runner/modelRetry.ts retries within a single provider. No automatic provider-fallback chain; you implement it as a custom ModelProvider wrapping multiple Model instances.

FallbackModel (models/fallback.py:69) wraps an ordered list of Model instances; on ResponseRejected or configured exception types falls through to the next. Pydantic AI Gateway adds load-balanced routing groups. Native providers across 14 vendors.
No retry-on-fallback-model mechanism. You write your own wrapper. 26 in-tree providers but no fallback or routing primitive.

ModelRetryStrategy (event_loop/_retry.py) is registered as a default hook with max_attempts=6, initial_delay=4s, max_delay=240s but retries the same model. For cross-provider fallback BYO via a custom Model wrapper or a hook that swaps agent.model on AfterModelCallEvent.exception.

DefaultModelRetryStrategy (strands-ts/src/retry/default-model-retry-strategy.ts) retries the same model on throttling/transient errors with exponential backoff. To swap providers on failure you write a custom ModelRetryStrategy or react to AfterModelCallEvent.error from a hook by mutating event.agent.model.

customProvider({ fallbackProvider }) (packages/ai/src/registry/custom-provider.ts) falls back to another provider only if the model id is missing, not on error. LanguageModelMiddleware.wrapGenerate/wrapStream lets you implement retry/fallback yourself. AI Gateway hosted product has it but not configurable from the SDK.

Each llmagent has its own Model model.LLM (llmagent.Config.Model). Different agents (supervisor vs workers) can use different models; within one agent the model is fixed. Cheap-for-triage pattern is architected as a triage agent delegating to a hard-work agent via agenttool or transfer_to_agent.

Model is assigned per agent (not per run), but additional task-specialist overrides exist: parser_model (agent.py:293), output_model (agent.py:297), reasoning_model (agent.py:192). agent.run(model=...) is not supported, so per-call routing requires multiple agents in a Team.

AgentBuilder::llm(Arc<dyn LLMProvider>) lets each agent take its own LLM, so different agents have different models. There is no built-in router that picks a model per task; the FallbackLayer and RetryLayer give composable primitives but no per-task selection primitive.

Sub-agent override via AgentDefinition.model (types.py:92). No per-call model option at run() level; the model is fixed on the session unless you transfer to a different sub-agent. Less flexible than the TypeScript SDK which exposes set_model at turn boundary.

Three layers: per-session Options.model (sdk.d.ts:1502), per-sub-agent AgentDefinition.model (sdk.d.ts:56), mid-session Query.setModel (sdk.d.ts:2076) at turn boundary. Aliases sonnet/opus/haiku supported. Cheap supervisor + expensive worker is straightforward.

Per-Agent llm setting and separately configurable manager_llm, function_calling_llm, planning_llm, chat_llm on Crew (crew.py:241-335). Native SDKs include OpenAI/Anthropic/Azure/Bedrock/Gemini plus LiteLLM. No first-party gateway that auto-routes by task class.

note: 3 — sub-agents plus WrapModel and skill middleware
details: Not first-class as a router, but achievable via different sub-agents (each ChatModelAgentConfig.Model independent) and WrapModel to swap models per turn. skill middleware can specify model: <name> per skill, fetched from ModelHub (adk/middlewares/skill/skill.go:79-88), giving per-skill model selection.

Per-call via ai.WithModelName(name) or ai.WithModel(modelRef) (go/ai/option.go:233-244). No registry/gateway; you write the dispatch logic in your code (e.g. switch on task type). Sub-agent overrides trivial since sub-agents are tools that call Generate.

Dynamic model selection (chat_agent_executor.py:325-356, 598-618). The model argument to create_react_agent can be a callable (state, runtime) -> BaseChatModel evaluated on every turn, enabling tier-based or task-based routing in code. Native via any langchain-* provider.

Each agent has its own llm field (base_agent.py:111-113). Different LLMs for each sub-agent in an AgentWorkflow (e.g. orchestrator Sonnet, workers Haiku). No first-party Router cheap-for-triage/expensive-for-hard abstraction; you build it as a routing tool or custom step.

note: 5 — dynamic model and streamOptions and prepareStep
details: model: DynamicArgument<MastraModelConfig> on Agent supports dynamic selection by requestContext (e.g. tier-based). Per-call streamOptions.model overrides. processInputStep can return { model: new model } mid-loop. Most flexible routing surface alongside vercel-ai and pydantic-ai.

No first-party gateway or router. You instantiate a different ChatClient per agent and select at construction time. For dynamic routing you write a custom IChatClient decorator. Sub-agent overrides are trivial via agent_as_tool composition.

Per-agent model override (Agent.model at src/agents/agent.py:311) plus per-run model override (RunConfig.model at src/agents/run_config.py:206) that forces every agent in the run to use a specific model. MultiProvider routes by string prefix (litellm/anthropic/...).

Per-agent (new Agent({ model })), per-run override (new Runner({ model }) or RunConfig.model), per-asTool override (Agent.asTool({ runConfig: { model } }) — see examples/agent-patterns/agents-as-tools.ts:33-39). No first-party registry but custom ModelProvider can route.

note: 5 — model kwarg on every run plus callable settings
details: model= kwarg on every run*() overrides the agent-level default. model_settings / AgentModelSettings (agent/__init__.py:177) accept a callable that receives RunContext and returns settings, enabling cheap-for-triage / expensive-for-hard-tasks routing inside one agent.

Not provided as a routing primitive. You build a different Agent per model (cheap = client.agent(GPT_4O_MINI), expensive = client.agent(GPT_5_2)) and choose which to call. OpenRouter provider gives per-call model selection at the API layer but framework has no first-party routing.

Per-agent. Each Agent instance has one model: Model. To route by task you build multiple Agent instances and switch with a manual dispatcher, or use the agent-as-tool pattern where each sub-agent uses a different model. No first-party gateway/router.

You pass model: Model | string per Agent (agent.ts:140). For per-task routing, instantiate multiple Agents (each with their own model) and dispatch to the right one, or use Graph/Swarm with different model on each node. No first-party gateway/router.

Three patterns: per-call model switch (pass different model to generate/streamText), prepareStep returning { model } to swap mid-loop, customProvider({ languageModels }) for aliases like 'chat-cheap' → gpt-4o-mini and 'chat-strong' → gpt-5. 50+ provider packages.

Each llmagent.New gets its own Model. A supervisor on Gemini Pro plus workers on Gemini Flash is the natural pattern. Different agents (supervisor vs workers, parent vs sub-agent) can use different models.
Each Team.members[i] is itself an Agent with its own model. Supervisor Claude / worker Haiku is straightforward. Composition via Team is the canonical pattern.

Every AgentBuilder takes its own llm naturally. You can wire Sonnet to a supervisor agent and Haiku to worker agents on the same runtime. No explicit override API; you just construct each sub-agent with the model you want.

AgentDefinition.model (types.py:92) is the first-class override (e.g. model='haiku'). Sonnet supervisor + Haiku workers is the canonical pattern. Reuses the same CLI session with sub-agent-scoped model.
AgentDefinition.model (sdk.d.ts:56) is exactly this; set to 'haiku' for cheap workers, leave the parent on 'opus'. Required-but-trivial for tenant cost control.
Each sub-agent has its own llm. Sonnet supervisor + Haiku workers crew is trivial via Process.hierarchical with manager_agent=supervisor. Native multi-model patterns documented.

Each ChatModelAgentConfig.Model is independent. NewChatModelAgent with claudeOpus for supervisor and claudeHaiku for workers, wired via SetSubAgents. Or via the prebuilt supervisor (adk/prebuilt/supervisor/supervisor.go).

Sub-agents are tools that internally call Generate; each can specify a different ai.WithModelName(...). Supervisor on gemini-2.5-pro, persona workers on gemini-2.5-flash is fully supported. No dedicated sub-agent abstraction but the pattern is trivial.
Each subgraph (sub-agent) is built with its own model argument. Sonnet-supervisor + Haiku-worker is the standard pattern. Dynamic model callable allows mixing too.

Each sub-agent in AgentWorkflow has its own llm (multi_agent_workflow.py:140 builds self.agents = {cfg.name: cfg for cfg in agents}; each cfg.llm is independent). Orchestrator on Sonnet, workers on Haiku is straightforward.
Every sub-agent declares its own model. Supervisor Opus + workers on Sonnet/Haiku is the canonical pattern. Dynamic model selection by requestContext makes per-tenant model routing easy.

Each sub-agent can be constructed with its own ChatClient so Sonnet supervisor + Haiku workers is straightforward via agent_as_tool composition. Implicit override since each agent is built independently.
Each Agent has its own model field, so a supervisor on gpt-5.1 can dispatch to a worker on gpt-5-mini via as_tool() or handoff. Per-run RunConfig.model can also force a uniform model across a run.

Agent.asTool({ runConfig: { model: 'gpt-5.4-mini' } }) — see examples/agent-patterns/agents-as-tools.ts:33-39. Handoff-target agents can each pin their own model. Per-agent and per-run also supported.

Each Agent instance carries its own model; agent delegation can mix any models. The doc warns USD computation may be limited if you mix providers (docs/multi-agent-applications.md:22-23) but the override itself is unrestricted.

Implicitly yes: each sub-agent is a separate Agent<M> and can be on a different model than the parent (parent wraps the sub-agent via agent/tool.rs:16-50). There's no explicit override API; you construct the sub-agent with the model you want.

Each sub-agent (whether as_tool(), Graph node, or Swarm node) carries its own model, so e.g. a Sonnet supervisor with Haiku workers is straightforward. Standard pattern across all multi-agent primitives.
Each sub-agent has its own model config: const supervisor = new Agent({ model: sonnet, tools: [haikuWorker] }) with haikuWorker on a different model. Standard pattern.
Trivial since sub-agents are BYO; you just instantiate each ToolLoopAgent with whatever model you want. No dedicated sub-agent abstraction but pattern is straightforward. customProvider aliases help.
